title: Modular Cognitive Architecture Emerges in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.13567v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The human brain exhibits a striking degree of functional specialization, with distinct networks supporting language, formal reasoning, reasoning about other minds, and reasoning about the physical world. Is this modular organization a fundamental principle of how intelligent systems must be built, or an evolutionary accident specific to biological brains? Here, we test whether a similar organization emerges in Large Language Models--another class of intelligent systems created through a very different optimization process. Using circuit analyses across N=46 tasks spanning four cognitive domains (language, formal reasoning, social reasoning, physical reasoning), we find that LLMs develop a modular architecture that mirrors the human brain: tasks drawing on the same network in humans recruit overlapping neurons in LLMs, whereas tasks drawing on different networks recruit distinct neurons. translated_title: 大型语言模型中涌现的模块化认知架构
translated_abstract: 摘要：arXiv:2608.13567v1 公告类型：新 摘要：人脑表现出显著的功能专门化程度，不同的网络支持语言、形式推理、关于他人心智的推理以及对物理世界的推理。这种模块化组织是智能系统必须如何构建的基本原理，还是生物大脑特有的进化偶然事件？在这里，我们测试了类似的组织是否在大型语言模型——另一类通过非常不同的优化过程创造的智能系统——中涌现。通过对跨越四个认知领域（语言、形式推理、社会推理、物理推理）的N=46个任务进行电路分析，我们发现大型语言模型发展出一种镜像人脑的模块化架构：在人脑中调用相同网络的任务在大型语言模型中招募重叠的神经元，而调用不同网络的任务则招募不同的神经元。大脑和大型语言模型中模块化的趋同涌现表明，这种组织可能是智能系统的一个普遍原则，而非生物进化的偶然结果。
tldr: 该论文发现大型语言模型通过电路分析，在语言、形式推理、社会推理和物理推理等任务中自发形成与人脑相似的模块化认知架构，表明模块化可能是智能系统的普遍原则。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that large language models spontaneously develop a modular cognitive architecture mirroring the human brain across language, formal, social, and physical reasoning tasks, suggesting modularity may be a universal principle of intelligent systems.
